_readme: Copied to /etc/stashling/stashling.json by bootstrap.sh. Edit that copy, not this one.
minRows is the most important field here and the only one you cannot guess. It is the
number below which a capture is treated as TRUNCATED rather than complete. It exists
because the characteristic failure of this whole design is silent: if the collection tab
is not the visible, active tab, a virtualized list materialises only its first screenful,
the row count stops growing, and the capture reports settled:true having collected maybe
7% of your list. Nothing errors. It merges cleanly into the store and looks like a quiet
day. So: run one sweep by hand, see how many rows it reports, and set minRows a little
under that. Re-check it when your list grows.
There is no entry URL in the connector itself. A connector declares match(url) and
instanceId(url) -- predicates that RECOGNISE a list page -- and nothing that says where
the page lives, because until now a human was always already on it. Hence this file.
MakerWorld URLs contain your own handle, so they could not be hard-coded anyway.
_extension: Where the unpacked extension is loaded from. Chrome derives an unpacked extension's id from
this path, which is how a sweep finds the extension while its service worker is ASLEEP --
and between sweeps it always is. If chrome://extensions shows a different id, put that id in
extensionId and the derivation is skipped.

targets._disabled_until: you replace YOUR-HANDLE below, then move this out of _readme order
targets.name: makerworld-likes

_politeness: A randomised gap between targets. The capture already randomises its own scroll intervals
because a metronome is the most legible bot signature there is; a perfectly regular sweep
undoes that at the next level up. The systemd timer adds a third layer of jitter.
Two values, milliseconds: the minimum and maximum wait.
_timeouts: collectTimeoutMs must stay under the MV3 service worker's five-minute-per-request ceiling
plus the time to parse and store. Beyond that Chrome kills the handler mid-run and tells
the caller nothing. YouTube's connector scrolls for at most 120s (autoScroll.maxMs), so
eight minutes is generous; if you raise maxMs, re-check this.
_blocked: If the final URL after redirects matches any of these, the sweep stops for that target and
reports needs-human instead of collecting a login wall. These are regexes, case-insensitive.
Leave the defaults unless a platform moves its sign-in path.
